name: Graph Theory
description: Graphs as mathematical objects: paths, connectivity, trees, matchings, flows, colouring, planarity and networks.

nodes.name: Graph basics
nodes.desc: Vertices, edges, degrees, the handshake lemma, subgraphs and directed versus undirected graphs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe graphs precisely using vertices, edges and degrees and apply the handshake lemma to simple counting problems.

nodes.name: Representations
nodes.desc: Adjacency matrices, adjacency lists and incidence matrices and their trade-offs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store a graph as an adjacency matrix, adjacency list or incidence matrix and pick one for a task.

nodes.name: Special graphs
nodes.desc: Complete, bipartite, regular, cycle, path, wheel and hypercube graphs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise standard graph families and state their vertex counts, edge counts and degree properties.

nodes.name: Isomorphism
nodes.desc: When two graphs are the same, graph invariants and automorphisms.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide whether two graphs are isomorphic using invariants and understand automorphisms as symmetries.
topics: Proving two graphs are not isomorphic

nodes.name: Walks & paths
nodes.desc: Walks, trails, paths, cycles, distance and diameter.
nodes.summary: You will be able to distinguish walks, trails, paths and cycles and compute distances, eccentricity and diameter.
topics: Counting walks with adjacency matrix powers

nodes.name: Connectivity
nodes.desc: Components, cut vertices, bridges, k-connectivity and Menger's theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse how well a graph holds together using components, cut vertices, bridges and Menger's theorem.

nodes.name: Euler & Hamilton
nodes.desc: Eulerian circuits, Hamiltonian cycles and conditions such as Dirac's and Ore's.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test for Eulerian circuits and apply sufficient conditions such as Dirac's and Ore's for Hamiltonian cycles.

nodes.name: BFS & DFS
nodes.desc: Breadth-first and depth-first search and what their trees reveal about structure.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run breadth-first and depth-first search and use their trees to reveal distances, components and cycles.

nodes.name: Directed graphs
nodes.desc: Strong connectivity, condensation, DAGs and topological orderings.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse directed graphs through strong connectivity and condensation and order DAGs topologically.

nodes.name: Trees
nodes.desc: Equivalent characterisations of trees, rooted trees and Cayley's formula.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove the equivalent characterisations of trees, work with rooted trees and count labelled trees with Cayley's formula.
topics: Leaves and the n minus 1 edges property

nodes.name: Spanning trees
nodes.desc: Minimum spanning trees and counting spanning trees with the matrix-tree theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find minimum spanning trees with Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms and count spanning trees with Kirchhoff's theorem.

nodes.name: Matchings
nodes.desc: Matchings and covers, Hall's marriage theorem and König's theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason about matchings and covers in bipartite graphs using Hall's and König's theorems.

nodes.name: Network flows
nodes.desc: Max-flow min-cut, augmenting paths and applications to matching.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute maximum flows with augmenting paths, prove optimality with min cuts and model matching as flow.

nodes.name: Graph colouring
nodes.desc: Chromatic number, greedy colouring, Brooks' theorem and edge colouring.
nodes.summary: You will be able to bound the chromatic number of a graph, colour it greedily and apply Brooks' and Vizing's theorems.

nodes.name: Planar graphs
nodes.desc: Euler's formula, Kuratowski's theorem and the four colour theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test and reason about planarity using Euler's formula, Kuratowski's theorem and colouring results for planar graphs.
topics: Euler's formula for connected planar graphs
The four and five colour theorems

nodes.name: Graph toolkit
nodes.desc: Implement a graph library with traversal, flow and colouring algorithms and tests.
nodes.summary: You will implement and test a small graph library with traversals, flow and colouring algorithms behind a clean interface.

nodes.name: Spectral graphs
nodes.desc: Adjacency and Laplacian eigenvalues and what they say about a graph.
nodes.summary: You will be able to relate adjacency and Laplacian eigenvalues to structural properties such as connectivity, bipartiteness and expansion.

nodes.name: Random graphs
nodes.desc: Erdos-Renyi graphs, thresholds and the giant component.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse Erdos-Renyi random graphs and explain threshold phenomena such as the emergence of a giant component.

nodes.name: Ramsey & extremal
nodes.desc: Ramsey numbers, Turan's theorem and extremal questions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to state and prove basic Ramsey bounds and Turan's theorem on the maximum edges without a clique.

nodes.name: Network analysis
nodes.desc: Centrality, PageRank and community detection in real networks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to measure importance and structure in real networks using centrality measures, PageRank and community detection.

nodes.name: Network study
nodes.desc: Analyse a real social or transport network and compare it with random models.
nodes.summary: You will analyse a real social or transport network and compare its statistics with those of random graph models.
